faq.q: How painful is a forearm tattoo?
faq.a: Most people describe the forearm as moderate compared with ribs or hands, but reports vary widely and depend on session length. Ask your artist what to expect for the exact position you have in mind.

faq.q: What size works best on the forearm?
faq.a: Most forearm pieces sit between 5 and 18 cm. Fine line work needs room to stay readable as it ages, so give detailed designs the upper half of that range.

faq.q: Can a forearm tattoo be covered for work?
faq.a: The inner forearm is easier to cover than the outer, and a long sleeve hides both. If your workplace has a policy, check it before you book rather than after.

faq.q: How long does a forearm tattoo take?
faq.a: A small piece can be under an hour; a detailed medium piece is usually 2-4 hours. Heavily shaded or wrap-around work is normally split across sessions.

faq.q: Should I choose the inner or outer forearm?
faq.a: The outer forearm is flatter and easier to read from the outside, the inner is more private and the skin is softer. Bring both options to your artist and ask which suits the design.
